title: Romance scams in practice
intro: Never pay someone you have not met. Decide what you would do in each moment from this module's lessons.

decisions.title: First message from Kamran
decisions.prompt: The first message. So far everything looks normal. What do you do with this message?

artifact.name: Kamran Aliyev
body: Hi! I came across your photos and really liked them. I am an engineer on an offshore oil platform and rarely get to Baku.

options.label: Check his photo with a reverse image search
Send my phone number and workplace

decisions.explain: Fake profiles often use someone else's photos; a reverse image search shows where a photo comes from.

decisions.title: Call from Nordhaven Clinic

artifact.name: Nordhaven Clinic
body: Doctor Helena Mart, Nordhaven Clinic, speaking. Kamran Aliyev had an accident and named you as his next of kin.

options.label: I want a video call with Kamran
What do you need? I will help

decisions.explain: A real hospital will not object to a video call. A scammer always finds a reason why it is impossible.

decisions.title: Kamran avoids video calls
decisions.prompt: Two weeks have passed. Messages arrive every day. What do you do with this message?

artifact.name: Kamran Aliyev
body: You are my first thought every morning.
I would love to, but the camera does not work on the platform and the internet is weak. I can only write.

decisions.explain: Avoiding video calls for weeks is a key sign of a fake profile.

decisions.title: Message from Elchin

artifact.name: Elchin
body: Shall we video call tonight at 8? Then we can meet at a cafe on Saturday.

decisions.explain: Offering a video call and a meeting in a public place is normal. That is exactly what a scammer avoids.

decisions.title: Message from Mark Leon

artifact.name: Mark Leon
body: To come and see you I need money for the visa, 600 AZN. I will pay it back as soon as I arrive, I promise.

decisions.explain: Someone you have never met asking for ticket, visa or customs money is a classic scam.
